bull.b: Strong sequential activation growth in the Balance and Active families indicates improving adoption of newer, higher-value products. If sustained, broader usage can strengthen Zepp’s ecosystem, support revenue growth, and improve product mix over the next several quarters.

Continued software development increases the usefulness of Zepp devices after purchase and gives the company more ways to differentiate its wearable ecosystem. Expanding training, recovery and navigation functionality can support retention and reinforce the value of future hardware launches.

Extending debt maturities reduces near-term repayment pressure and gives management more time to execute its operating recovery. This does not remove leverage risk, but it can improve financial flexibility while the company works to restore profitability and cash generation.

bear.b: Zepp has not re-established the sustainable profitability seen in 2020–2021, despite gross-margin improvement and narrower losses versus 2024. Continued operating and net losses weaken resilience, restrict internally funded investment, and make the turnaround dependent on further execution.

Negative operating and free cash flow across consecutive years shows that the business is not reliably funding operations internally. If losses persist, ongoing cash consumption can reduce financial flexibility and increase reliance on balance-sheet resources to support product and market investments.

Longer component lead times and constrained availability can prevent Zepp from fully converting product demand into revenue. These conditions also complicate inventory planning and, alongside higher component costs, can pressure gross margins and make operational improvement less predictable.
